title: Cardinality of a shifted coordinate set
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S$ be a set of coordinates in $\\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Shift each element of $S$ up by one to obtain a subset of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$. The resulting set has the same cardinality as $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a finite set of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
